stories.title: A studio cut its own site's emissions by two thirds and treated carbon as a creative constraint
stories.blurb: MEK found its own website emitted more carbon than 76.5% of pages tested, then rebuilt it: AVIF instead of high-res JPG, almost all motion and video removed, dark mode instead of a white interface, and a hard look at the webfont. Emissions fell from 1.21 g to 0.42 g of CO2 per page view, and the studio kept a Google font rather than accept Arial, which is the honest part of the piece.

sources.name: Design Week
sources.headline: No fonts on a dead planet: a website case study

stories.title: One worked example that carries a UX case from goal to ROI number
stories.blurb: Alex Williams runs a single invented B2B SaaS onboarding redesign all the way through: defining business value, accounting for cost, testing causality, and arriving at a number. The point is that the figures connect across every step, which is what a framework usually fails to show.

sources.name: Smashing Magazine
sources.headline: Building A UX ROI Case That Survives The Boardroom

stories.title: Eight patterns for voice AI interfaces, each with its own failure mode
stories.blurb: Sharang Sharma maps voice AI experiences into named patterns, from avatar video call to strict turn-by-turn to AI phone call, and for each one names the perceived agent role, the key design decisions and the limits. Turn-by-turn deliberately has no face and no barge-in, which is why it only fits tutoring and interview prep.

stories.title: Branding has no shared vocabulary, so one agency published its own
stories.blurb: LETTER A has put out a running dictionary of the terms branding agencies create, discuss and deliver, on the argument that everyone uses them slightly differently and nobody notices until the client sees something they did not expect. Useful mostly as a shared reference to point a client at before the deliverables list is agreed.

sources.name: PRINT Magazine
sources.headline: Don’t Know the Difference Between Brand Guidelines and a Brand Book? There’s a Branding Dictionary For That

stories.title: Whistles cast its 50th anniversary campaign from fly-posters instead of a model agency
stories.blurb: Agency Weirdo covered London with unbranded posters asking what open-mindedness means, got more than 2,000 replies, and cut them to 50 women aged 19 to 72 shot in a single day. The casting mechanic doubles as the research behind the new brand platform, Designed for an Open Mind.

sources.headline: Whistles marks 50 years by casting 50 customers found through mysterious fly-posters across London

sources.name: Roastbrief
sources.headline: Whistles marks 50 years with bold brand relaunch, new ‘Designed for an Open Mind’ brand platform and a campaign starring 50 open-minded customers

stories.title: Mother Design repositioned a psychic platform by refusing the wellness look
stories.blurb: Research outside the category showed people turn to AI and coaching for daily guidance but are really after perspective, so Keen was moved from predicting the future to helping people get unstuck. Creative director Jo Tulej names the default the studio walked away from: white space, muted palettes, rounded type, gentle promises.

sources.name: Creative Boom
sources.headline: Mother Design gives psychic platform Keen a folk-art rebrand that takes on minimalist wellness

stories.title: Share of voice is measured to the decimal, the sound inside it is picked by feel
stories.blurb: Shai Hirschon argues the ESOV framework assumes Monday's spot is recognisably the same brand as Wednesday's, which visual identity is built to honour and music is not. A typical brand's year contains acoustic folk, electronic textures and library cues from three production houses, so the compounding the model depends on leaks out through the speakers.

sources.name: Brandingmag
sources.headline: Sound Decoded: Share of Voice Has a Sound Problem

stories.title: A second mathematician asks OpenAI to prove his work was not in the training data
stories.blurb: Andreas Thom says his own ChatGPT interactions may have fed one of the ten results OpenAI announced last month, in his own field of non-sofic groups. OpenAI quietly amended the writeup after criticism that it failed to credit recent work by Thom and Gábor Kun, which is the provenance problem every creative trade is now having in its own language.

sources.name: The Verge
sources.headline: Mathematicians want proof OpenAI didn’t use their work

stories.title: Universal licenses its catalogue to ElevenLabs for a remix platform artists can opt into
stories.blurb: A multiyear licensing deal lets users build remixes and mashups from UMG's catalogue, with participation left to each artist. It sits alongside UMG's Udio platform and deals with Spotify, Nvidia and Klay, so the licensed route is becoming the industry's default answer rather than an experiment.

sources.name: The Verge
sources.headline: Universal Music is launching an AI music platform with ElevenLabs

stories.title: Slack will generate dashboards and microsites inside the channel where the data already is
stories.blurb: Slackforce Surfaces lets you describe a report, poll, dashboard or presentation to Slackbot, which pulls from conversations and connected apps like Drive or Salesforce, then pins the result to a channel for others to use and comment on. It is available to all workspaces with Slackbot enabled, free tier included.

sources.name: The Verge
sources.headline: Slack can now vibe-code interactive charts and reports inside chats

stories.title: Most of AUTOMATIC1111 rebuilt as a node graph you can duplicate and rewire
stories.blurb: Workflow1111 is eleven media pipelines across seventy-three nodes on a single Gradio canvas: text-to-image, hi-res fix, img2img, prompt-matrix grids, VLM interrogate, detection-to-inpaint masks, ControlNet-style annotators, background removal, PNG Info and image-to-video. Runs on your own Hugging Face quota, and the Space can be duplicated and rebuilt for your own pipeline.
